title: Advantages and Limitations of PHP
learning_outcomes: Explain what advantages and limitations of php contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: accessibility and hosting availability.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: PHP runs in the PHP runtime and is often used to generate dynamic web responses and command-line output. In a normal web request, the browser receives the response, not the original PHP source. In this lesson, focus on accessibility and hosting availability; then compare it with built-in web development functionality. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use advantages and limitations of php when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: PHP runs in the PHP runtime and is often used to generate dynamic web responses and command-line output. In a normal web request, the browser receives the response, not the original PHP source. For advantages and limitations of php, begin with accessibility and hosting availability. Also distinguish built-in web development functionality; ecosystem and package availability; runtime and deployment considerations. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content.task: Create a second small example for advantages and limitations of php that demonstrates "accessibility and hosting availability". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of accessibility and hosting availability.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
